title: Understanding Elementary Shapes
description: Class 6 IMO — Understanding elementary shapes: classifying triangles by sides and angles, quadrilaterals, polygons, and 3D shapes with their faces, edges and vertices.

topics.title: Classifying Triangles
topics.concept: Triangles are named by their sides: scalene (no equal sides), isosceles (2 equal sides) and equilateral (3 equal sides). They are also named by their angles: acute (all angles < 90°), right (one 90° angle) and obtuse (one angle > 90°).

examples.problem: What do we call a triangle with a 90° angle?
What do we call a triangle with all sides equal?

quiz.q: A triangle with all angles less than 90° is ___ ?
quiz.explanation: All angles under 90° make an acute triangle.

quiz.q: A triangle with exactly 2 equal sides is ___ ?
quiz.explanation: Two equal sides make an isosceles triangle.

topics.title: Quadrilaterals & Polygons
topics.concept: Quadrilaterals have 4 sides: square, rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram and trapezium (exactly one pair of parallel sides). A polygon is a closed shape with straight sides; a pentagon has 5 sides and a hexagon has 6. A regular polygon has all sides and angles equal.

examples.problem: What is a polygon with 5 sides called?
Which quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides?

recap: Quadrilaterals: square, rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram, trapezium.
Pentagon = 5 sides; hexagon = 6 sides; regular = all sides/angles equal.

quiz.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
A quadrilateral with all sides equal and 4 right angles is a ___ ?
quiz.explanation: Equal sides plus right angles make a square.

topics.title: 3D Shapes: Faces, Edges & Vertices
topics.concept: Solid (3D) shapes have faces (flat surfaces), edges (where faces meet) and vertices (corners). A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. A cone has 2 faces, 1 edge and 1 vertex, while a sphere has 1 curved face, 0 edges and 0 vertices.

examples.problem: How many faces does a cube have?
How many vertices does a cone have?

recap: Cone: 2 faces, 1 edge, 1 vertex; sphere: 1 face, 0 edges, 0 vertices.

quiz.q: How many edges does a cuboid have?
How many vertices does a sphere have?

questions.q: Which is the odd one out (three are quadrilaterals)?
questions.explanation: A triangle has 3 sides; the others are quadrilaterals.

questions.q: Pentagon is to 5 as hexagon is to ___ ?
A triangle with one right angle is a ___ triangle.
questions.explanation: A 90° angle makes a right triangle.

questions.q: Which of these is a regular polygon (all sides equal)?
questions.explanation: A square has all sides and angles equal, so it is regular.

questions.explanation: One pair of parallel sides makes a trapezium.
